name: Huntress (AVV)
body:
The huntress is an elite frontierswoman and master of wilderness survival. She is athletic, wise, and an expert archer. All huntresses are trained in sniping and ambush.

As civilians, they serve their communities as deerstalkers, trappers, and wilderness guides. In a military role, they often serve as scouts, guerrillas, and commandoes.

Huntresses often travel the most dangerous and remote reaches of the wild lands and are likely to encounter chthonic monsters and bizarre creatures of a bygone age. As a result, they may have a special animosity or divine purpose in hunting a particular type of creature. Other huntresses, however, specialize in stalking humans.

Role: The huntress is a deft skirmisher, either in melee or at range, capable of skillfully dancing in and out of battle. Her abilities allow her to deal significant harm to specific types of foes, but her skills are valuable against all manner of enemies.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d10.

Class Skills

The huntress’s class skills are Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), Stealth (Dex), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Table: The Huntress

6	+6/+1	+5	+5	+2	Combat style feat

8	+8/+3	+6	+6	+2	Swift tracker, 2nd favored terrain, combat style feat

10	+10/+5	+7	+7	+3	3rd favored enemy, combat style feat
Class Features

All of the following are class features of the huntress.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A huntress is proficient with all simple and martial weapons and with light armor, medium armor, and shields (except tower shields).

Favored Enemy (Ex)

At 1st level, a huntress selects a creature type from the Huntress Favored Enemies Table. She gains a +2 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks against creatures of her selected type. Likewise, she gets a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against them.

A huntress may make Knowledge skill checks untrained when attempting to identify these creatures.

At 5th level, the huntress may select an additional favored enemy. In addition, the bonus against the previous favored enemy (or the one just selected, if so desired) increases by +2.

If the huntress chooses humanoids or outsiders as a favored enemy, she must also choose an associated subtype, as indicated on the table below. (Note that there are other types of humanoid to choose from—those called out specifically on the table below are merely the most common.) If a specific creature falls into more than one category of favored enemy, the huntress’s bonuses do not stack; she simply uses whichever bonus is higher.

Track (Ex)

A huntress adds half her level (minimum 1) to Survival skill checks made to follow tracks.

Wild Empathy (Ex)

A huntress can improve the initial attitude of an animal. This ability functions just like a Diplomacy check to improve the attitude of a person (see Using Skills). The huntress rolls 1d20 and adds her huntress level and her Charisma bonus to determine the wild empathy check result. The typical domestic animal has a starting attitude of indifferent, while wild animals are usually unfriendly.

To use wild empathy, the huntress and the animal must be within 30 feet of one another under normal visibility conditions. Generally, influencing an animal in this way takes 1 minute, but, as with influencing people, it might take more or less time.

The huntress can also use this ability to influence a magical beast with an Intelligence score of 1 or 2, but she takes a –4 penalty on the check.

Combat Style Feat (Ex)

At 2nd level, a huntress must select one of two combat styles to pursue: archery or two-weapon combat. The huntress’s expertise manifests in the form of bonus feats at 2nd, 6th, and 10th level. She can choose feats from her selected combat style, even if she does not have the normal prerequisites.

If the huntress selects archery, she can choose from the following list whenever she gains a combat style feat: Far Shot, Point-Blank Shot, Precise Shot, and Rapid Shot. At 6th level, she adds Improved Precise Shot and Manyshot to the list. At 10th level, she adds Pinpoint Targeting and Shot on the Run to the list.

If the huntress selects two-weapon combat, she can choose from the following list whenever she gains a combat style feat: Double Slice, Improved Shield Bash, Quick Draw, and Two-Weapon Fighting. At 6th level, she adds Improved Two-Weapon Fighting and Two-Weapon Defense to the list. At 10th level, she adds Greater Twoweapon Fighting and Two-Weapon Rend to the list.

The benefits of the huntress’s chosen style feats apply only when she wears light, medium, or no armor.

She loses all benefits of her combat style feats when wearing heavy armor. Once a huntress selects a combat style, it cannot be changed.

Endurance

A huntress gains Endurance as a bonus feat at 3rd level.

Prohibited Favored Enemies

Several creatures from the standard Favored Enemy list are not included here. In most cases, this is because the creature in question does not exist in this setting (such as orcs and goblins). Although oozes exist, they are so rare that huntresses cannot have them as a favored enemy.

Favored Terrain (Ex)

At 3rd level, a huntress may select a type of terrain from the Favored Terrains table.

The huntress gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks and Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks when she is in this terrain. A huntress favored terraintraveling through her favored terrain normally leaves no trail and cannot be tracked (though she may leave a trail if she so chooses).

At 8th level, the huntress may select an additional favored terrain. In addition, at each such interval, the skill bonus and initiative bonus in any one favored terrain (including the one just selected, if so desired), increases by +2.

If a specific terrain falls into more than one category of favored terrain, the huntress’s bonuses do not stack; she simply uses whichever bonus is higher.

Hunter’s Bond (Ex)

At 4th level, a huntress forms a bond with her hunting companions. This bond can take one of two forms. Once the form is chosen, it cannot be changed. The first is a bond to her companions. This bond allows her to spend a move action to grant half her favored enemy bonus against a single target of the appropriate type to all allies within 30 feet who can see or hear her. This bonus lasts for a number of rounds equal to the huntress’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

This bonus does not stack with any favored enemy bonuses possessed by her allies; they use whichever bonus is higher.

The second option is to form a close bond with an animal companion. A huntress who selects an animal companion can choose from the following list: badger, bird, camel, cat (small), dire rat, dog, horse, pony, snake (viper or constrictor), or wolf. If the campaign takes place wholly or partly in an aquatic environment, the huntress may choose a shark instead.

This animal is a loyal companion that accompanies the huntress on her adventures as appropriate for its kind. A huntress’s animal companion shares her favored enemy and favored terrain bonuses.

This ability functions like the druid animal companion ability (which is part of the Nature Bond class feature), except that the huntress’s effective druid level is equal to her huntress level – 3.

Woodland Stride (Ex)

Starting at 7th level, a huntress may move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at her normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that are enchanted or magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect her.

Swift Tracker (Ex)

Beginning at 8th level, a huntress can move at her normal speed while using Survival to follow tracks without taking the normal –5 penalty. She takes only a –10 penalty (instead of the normal –20) when moving at up to twice normal speed while tracking.

Evasion (Ex)

When she reaches 9th level, a huntress can avoid even magical and unusual attacks with great agility. If she makes a successful Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, she instead takes no damage.

Evasion can be used only if the huntress is wearing light armor, medium armor, or no armor. A helpless huntress does not gain the benefit of evasion.

Favored Terrains
Cold (ice, glaciers, snow and tundra)
Desert (sand and wasteland)
Forest (coniferous and deciduous) Jungle
Mountain (including hillls) Plains
Planes (Asgard, Olympus, Jotunheim, Alfheim, Svartalfheim, Vanaheim, or the Underworld)

Urban (buildings, streets, and sewers)
